notes: Site situations, played on a visit to a point of interest and never drawn on the road (design §6). The POI types in data/procedural/poi-types.json name them. Shrines trade gold for Inspiration (a fixed offering) or a day for healing (a Religion check). Landmarks offer a risky vantage point (Perception for Edge) and then lore (History for a journal line and a little gold). Wonders are one click and flavour only (no rewards). A boon (an offering, a vigil, healing, lore with a find) has `siteReady`: a site gives one boon per BOON_COOLDOWN_DAYS (30) days. Lairs (Plan 3b B3) are hostile tugs of war: an approach that sets the footing, the assault, and the leader (high stakes); success clears the lair (clearPoi) for gold, a failure drives the party off with HP and days lost and the lair stays. Dungeons run entrance, hazard, a high-stakes guardian and the vault, which clears them. Lone experts are services the party can come back to: paid training (gold, days and someone untrained), paid knowledge (only while something is left to learn: `undiscovered`) and paid care are always on offer; a check to earn it free, a free rest (a quarter of everyone's HP and a level of exhaustion, with `siteReady`, so once per BOON_COOLDOWN_DAYS at that site), and a way to just talk. Quest sites give a clue and log a hook for Plan 4. Plan 4 (B5): the lair leaders' fight and the dungeon vaults pay part of their gold as precious goods (relics, gems, luxuries; the kobold seam adds heavy silver as metal), so loot has to be carried home and sold where it is wanted; the nominal value is about 1.3–2.5× the old gold, to be tuned with the I1 economy report. Consumables: a smoke flask and a healing kit in the goblin warren, alchemist's fire in the kobold mine, and an arcana warding against the hag coven and the barrow lord. Plan 5a: six clearings also loot an accessory (the `accessory` effect): the orc war-chief, the cult manor and hag hollow leaders, the barrow's unbound coffer and the keep's ledger give tier 1, the drake's hoard tier 2. Written by Claude.

start.text: A roofless shrine of fieldstone stands where two tracks meet. Someone still sweeps it: there are fresh flowers on the altar, and a cracked bowl for coins.

options.label: Leave an offering and pray
options.description: 5 gold in the bowl.

outcome.text: The coins ring in the bowl. For a moment the wind drops, and the quiet feels like an answer.

options.label: Keep a vigil through the night
options.description: Costs a day. A good vigil mends body and spirit.

fail.text: {actor} says the old words until they stop meaning anything. The night is cold and long.

partial.text: The night passes quietly, and you rise a little mended.

success.text: {actor} keeps the rites the old way. You wake more rested than you have in weeks.

outcome.text: You bow your heads and walk on.

start.text: A mossy well stands under a stone hood, carved with a saint nobody remembers. The water is cold and very clear, and someone has hung a new rope.

options.label: Drop in a coin and make a wish
options.description: 3 gold down the well.

outcome.text: The coin falls a long way. You hear it land, and then, faintly, something like a laugh.

options.label: Bless the water and bathe
options.description: Said right, the old blessing washes weariness away. The stones are slick.

fail.text: The water is only cold. {actor} slips on the wet stones climbing out.

partial.text: The cold drives the ache out of {actor}'s bones, if no one else's.

success.text: {actor} says the blessing, and the water seems to brighten. Everyone climbs out lighter.

options.label: Drink, fill your skins and go

outcome.text: The water tastes of iron and stone. It is the best you have had in days.

start.text: A chapel has sunk to its windows in the mire. Black water fills the nave, and candle stubs still stand along the dry gallery. Something has kept them lit.

options.label: Light a candle and leave an offering
options.description: 5 gold on the gallery rail.

outcome.text: Your candle takes at once. Out over the water the other flames gutter and go out, one by one, as if satisfied.

options.label: Say the rites for the drowned
options.description: The dead here want remembering. Doing it badly offends them.

fail.text: {actor} stumbles over the words. The water stirs, and cold hands catch at your ankles all the way out.

partial.text: The water stills. You rest a while on the gallery and leave a little mended.

success.text: {actor} names the drowned as best anyone can. A warmth fills the nave, and your weariness lifts.

options.label: Fish the offerings out of the font
options.description: Coins glint in the drowned font. Taking them is not polite.

fail.text: Something under the water takes hold of {actor}'s wrist and does not let go for far too long.

partial.text: {actor} comes up with a handful of green coins and a chill that won't shift.

success.text: {actor} works quickly and quietly, and comes up with a fistful of old silver.

options.label: Leave the dead to their water

outcome.text: You back out along the gallery, and nobody looks at the water.

start.text: Nine grey stones stand in a ring on the crest, leaning like tired old men. The tallest has a ledge cut into it, and the rest are covered in worn carvings.

options.label: Climb the tall stone and look around
options.description: A good look gives you Edge on the carvings. A fall hurts.

fail.text: {actor} slips off the wet ledge and lands badly.

partial.text: The view is fine, but it tells {actor} nothing.

success.text: From the ledge {actor} sees the stones line up with the hills around: the carvings are a map.

outcome.text: You walk the ring, stone by stone.
You leave the stones to the wind.

carvings.text: The carvings are old, older than the kingdoms. Someone patient could make sense of them.

options.label: Read the carvings
options.description: A good reading is worth knowing, and maybe more.

fail.text: {actor} traces the marks for an hour and makes nothing of them.

partial.text: {actor} makes out a name, and a warning.

effects.text: The standing stones remember a king buried upright, so that he would never kneel, and warn against waking him.

success.text: {actor} reads the dedication, and a line telling where the offerings were buried. A little digging turns up a pot of old coins.

effects.text: The standing stones remember a king buried upright, so that he would never kneel, and warn against waking him.

outcome.text: You leave the stones as you found them.

start.text: A bell tower leans out of the reeds, the village it served long gone under the water. The bell still hangs in it, green with age. On still nights, people say, it rings by itself.

options.label: Climb to the belfry and look out
options.description: Rotten stairs. A good look gives you Edge on what lies below.

fail.text: A stair gives way under {actor}, who drops into the black water among the timbers.

partial.text: {actor} sees only reeds and water, and climbs back down.

success.text: From the belfry {actor} can make out the drowned streets under the water, and the tower's own carvings from above.

outcome.text: You wade out, waist-deep and cold, to the tower door.
You leave the tower to the reeds.

bell.text: Names and dates are cut into the bell and into the stones of the tower: a whole village, remembered by its bell.

options.label: Piece together the village's story
options.description: A good reading is worth knowing, and maybe more.

fail.text: The names mean nothing to {actor}, and the water is getting colder.

partial.text: {actor} reads enough to know how the village died.

effects.text: The drowned bell tower served a village that went under in one night when the dykes broke.

success.text: {actor} pieces it together: the dykes were broken on purpose, and the reeve fled with the tithe. His strongbox is still wedged in the belfry.

effects.text: The drowned bell tower served a village that went under in one night when its reeve broke the dykes and fled with the tithe.

options.label: Leave the names to the water

outcome.text: You wade back to dry land without a word.

start.text: A watchtower of some older kingdom stands broken-topped on the height, its stair spiralling up to nothing. On a clear day, they say, you can see three lands from the top.

options.label: Climb to the top and look out
options.description: A good look gives you Edge on what the walls say. The stair crumbles.

fail.text: The stair crumbles under {actor}'s feet. It is a bad fall.

partial.text: Haze hides the far lands. {actor} climbs down none the wiser.

success.text: From the top {actor} sees the old border road, and where the soldiers' marks on the walls point.

outcome.text: You duck into the old guardroom.
You leave the tower to the crows.

walls.text: Soldiers left their marks on the guardroom walls: names, tallies, a rough map of a border that is long gone.

options.label: Make sense of the marks
options.description: A good reading is worth knowing, and maybe more.

fail.text: {actor} reads names and tallies, and nothing more.

partial.text: {actor} works out which kingdom held the tower, and what it feared.

effects.text: Soldiers' marks in a broken watchtower show the border as it ran two kingdoms ago, and the raids it was built to watch for.

success.text: {actor} spots a tally that isn't a tally: a soldier's note of where he hid his pay. It is still there.

effects.text: Soldiers' marks in a broken watchtower show the border as it ran two kingdoms ago, and the raids it was built to watch for.

outcome.text: You leave the tower to the crows.

start.text: A waterfall drops from the cliff into a deep pool, and the water glows a soft blue-green, brighter as dusk comes on. Fish like lanterns turn in the pool. Nobody fills a waterskin here, and nobody can say why not.

outcome.text: When night falls the whole gorge is lit from below. You sleep to the sound of it, and wake with the light still in your eyes.

start.text: Out in the waste the sand has turned to glass across a whole valley, rippled like a frozen pond. At noon it blinds you. At sunset, they say, it burns.

outcome.text: For a few minutes the whole valley is on fire, red and gold. Then it is only glass again, ticking as it cools.

start.text: The ribs of something enormous arch out of the ground, bleached white and taller than a house. The old track runs right through them.

outcome.text: Your voices echo strangely between the bones. On the far side everyone is quiet for a while, and nobody says what they were thinking.

start.text: Smoke from a dozen cookfires hangs over a stockade of sharpened logs. Skulls on poles mark the edge of the camp, and the war-drums have not stopped since you came in sight.

options.label: Creep up through the gully
options.description: Do it well and you strike with the Edge. Get spotted and you go in Exposed.

fail.text: A camp dog starts barking. Horns answer from inside the stockade.

partial.text: You reach the stockade, though a sentry looks your way twice.

success.text: {actor} brings you to the foot of the stockade unseen, close enough to count the sentries.

options.label: Stampede their horses through the camp
options.description: Thin the camp out before you go in. A botch rouses everyone.

fail.text: The horses scatter the wrong way, and the whole camp comes awake.

partial.text: The horses bolt, but around the camp rather than through it.

success.text: {actor} sets the herd running. It tramples through the cookfires, and half the warriors chase after it.

outcome.text: You walk up to the gate with your weapons out. The drums stop.
You back away into the hills. The drums follow you for a long time.

assault.text: Orc warriors pour out of the gate, bellowing, with axes and boar-spears. Behind them a huge orc in a bear's skull roars them on.

options.label: Fight
options.description: Success clears the lair. Do badly and they rally around their leader; fail and they drive you off, and the lair stays.

critFail.text: The rush overwhelms you. You run for your lives and leave half your packs in the mud.

fail.text: There are too many of them. You fight your way clear and run, and the camp jeers you all the way down the valley.

partial.text: You cut through the first rush, bleeding, but the war-chief rallies the rest around the war totem.

success.text: The warriors break and scatter into the hills. In the war-chief's tent you find the camp's plunder, and nobody left to guard it.

options.label: Challenge the war-chief to single combat
options.description: Orcs respect a challenge. Meet their chief on your terms, or be laughed at.

fail.text: They laugh at {actor}, and a thrown spear nearly ends the conversation.

partial.text: The warriors hold back, unsure, and the war-chief comes forward himself.

success.text: {actor} bellows the challenge. The warriors stand back and make a ring, grinning: this they want to see.

options.label: Fall back to the gully
options.description: Get out with a few cuts. The lair stays.

outcome.text: You fight a retreat to the gully and lose them in the dark.

chief.text: The war-chief plants his feet by the war totem, a cleaver in each hand, and the camp holds its breath.

options.label: Fight the war-chief
options.description: Win and the lair is broken for good. Lose and you are driven off, and the lair stays.

fail.text: He batters {actor} senseless. You drag them away while the camp howls.

partial.text: {actor} brings him down at a terrible cost. The camp breaks up around his body.

success.text: The war-chief goes down, and the camp goes with him. By nightfall the stockade is burning, the warriors are scattered over three valleys, and their plunder is yours.

options.label: Break their nerve
options.description: Shame them into leaving. No plunder, but no one else gets hurt either.

fail.text: The war-chief only laughs, and his warriors close in again.

partial.text: They waver, but they don't run. You get out while they argue.

success.text: {actor} roars over the war-chief's body-guards until they waver, then run. The war-chief follows them, cursing. The camp burns behind them.

options.label: Back away while you can
options.description: Break off while you still can. The lair stays.

outcome.text: You give ground step by step, and they let you go.

start.text: A hillside riddled with holes, and every hole stinks. Bones and bright rags are strung across the thorn bushes, and somewhere underground goblins are squabbling.

options.label: Find their back door
options.description: Do it well and you strike with the Edge. Get spotted and you go in Exposed.

fail.text: A goblin lookout spots you from a thorn bush and shrieks the alarm.

partial.text: There are a dozen holes. You pick one and hope.

success.text: {actor} spots a bolt-hole they forgot to guard. You can come at them from behind.

options.label: Smoke them out
options.description: Fight them in the open instead of in their tunnels. Botch it and you go in choking.

fail.text: The smoke blows back in your faces, and the goblins are ready for you.

partial.text: Some smoke goes in, and some goblins come out, angrier than before.

success.text: {actor} stuffs wet bracken into the holes and lights it. Goblins come boiling out, coughing and half blind.

options.label: Drop a smoke flask down the main hole (1 alchemicals)
options.description: An alchemist's smoke does what wet bracken only might: a sure Edge.

outcome.text: Yellow smoke pours out of every hole on the hill at once. The goblins come boiling out, weeping and blind.
You get down on your knees and crawl into the stink.
You leave the hill to the goblins, and their jeering follows you.

assault.text: The tunnels are low and crooked, and goblins come at you from every side with knives, darts and a pot of something boiling.

options.label: Fight
options.description: Success clears the lair. Do badly and they rally around their leader; fail and they drive you off, and the lair stays.

critFail.text: Something falls on you in the dark. You scramble out without your purse, and the goblins have a party.

fail.text: You crawl out bleeding from a dozen small cuts, and the jeering follows you all the way down the hill.

partial.text: You beat back the mob, cut a dozen times, and the survivors bolt for their boss's den.

success.text: The warren empties out the far side of the hill. Their hoard of stolen trinkets is yours, and the holes are quiet.

options.label: Bring the tunnel roof down
options.description: Collapse the warren on them. Pick the wrong prop and it falls on you.

fail.text: {actor} pulls the wrong prop, and the roof comes down on them instead.

partial.text: Part of the tunnel falls in, and the fight moves deeper.

success.text: {actor} finds the rotten prop holding up the main burrow. Down it comes, and the goblins flee to their boss.

options.label: Bind your wounds and go again (1 healing)
options.description: A breather in a side tunnel, and a kit's worth of bandages.

outcome.text: You hold a side tunnel long enough to bind the worst of the cuts. Then back into the dark.

options.label: Back out of the tunnels
options.description: Get out with a few cuts. The lair stays.

outcome.text: You back out the way you came, and the goblins don't follow into the daylight.

chief.text: In the deepest den a fat goblin boss sits on a heap of stolen saddles, with a mangy worg growling at his feet.

options.label: Fight the boss and his worg
options.description: Win and the lair is broken for good. Lose and you are driven off, and the lair stays.

fail.text: The worg drags {actor} down, and you have to cut your way out of the den.

partial.text: {actor} ends up bitten to the bone, but the boss is dead and the tribe is gone.

success.text: The worg runs and the boss dies on his saddles. The rest of the tribe scatters, and his heap of stolen goods is yours: coin, and a bale of silks still in a merchant's wrapping.

options.label: Promise him a better hole elsewhere
options.description: Talk him into moving on. No plunder, no more blood.

fail.text: He doesn't believe a word, and sets the worg on you.

partial.text: He believes half of it, and throws you a sack of junk to go away.

success.text: {actor} tells him of a valley full of fat sheep and no soldiers. He packs his saddles and leads his tribe off over the hill, to be someone else's problem.

options.label: Back away while you can
options.description: Break off while you still can. The lair stays.

outcome.text: You give ground step by step, and the boss is happy to let you go.

start.text: A burnt-out farmstead with a new roof on the barn. There are horses in the paddock, washing on the line, and a lookout in the dovecote who thinks you can't see him.

options.label: Take the lookout quietly
options.description: Do it well and you strike with the Edge. Get spotted and you go in Exposed.

fail.text: The lookout sees you coming and rings a pot-bell for all he's worth.

partial.text: You get close, but the lookout is already climbing down to warn the others.

success.text: {actor} is up the dovecote ladder and has a hand over the lookout's mouth before he knows it.

options.label: Pose as buyers for stolen goods
options.description: Get inside before the fight starts. If they see through you, they're ready.

fail.text: One of them knows your face from the road.

partial.text: They let you into the yard, but nobody puts their weapons away.

success.text: {actor} haggles like a born fence. They wave you into the barn, weapons sheathed.

outcome.text: You walk across the yard in plain sight.
You leave the farmstead to the outlaws and take the long way round.

assault.text: Outlaws spill out of the barn with crossbows and boar-spears, shouting for their captain.

options.label: Fight
options.description: Success clears the lair. Do badly and they rally around their leader; fail and they drive you off, and the lair stays.

critFail.text: A bolt in the thigh and a spear in the pack. You lose your purse getting over the fence.

fail.text: Crossbow bolts drive you back across the yard and over the fence. The outlaws don't bother to chase you.

partial.text: The outlaws fall back to the barn, where their captain is buckling on her sword.

success.text: The outlaws break and scatter. In the hayloft is a summer of road tolls, and nobody coming back for it.

options.label: Scatter their horses
options.description: Cut off their escape and break their spirit. Horses kick.

fail.text: A horse kicks {actor} into the trough, and the outlaws laugh as they reload.

partial.text: Some of the horses bolt, and the outlaws fall back to the barn.

success.text: {actor} opens the paddock and sends the horses galloping. Without them the outlaws can't run, and they know it.

options.label: Fall back over the fence
options.description: Get out with a few cuts. The lair stays.

outcome.text: You fight a retreat across the yard and over the fence.

chief.text: The bandit captain steps out of the barn, cloak thrown back, a sword in her hand and the road's tolls in a chest behind her.

options.label: Fight the captain
options.description: Win and the lair is broken for good. Lose and you are driven off, and the lair stays.

fail.text: She is better than {actor}, much better. You get out alive only because she lets you.

partial.text: {actor} trades cut for cut with her until she falls. Her outlaws scatter, but most of the chest goes with them.

success.text: The captain falls in the barn door. Her outlaws throw down their weapons and run, and her chest of tolls is yours. Under the coins lie a merchant's silks, never sold.

options.label: Offer her a chance to ride away
options.description: Talk her off the roads. No plunder, and she lives to rob elsewhere.

fail.text: She has heard that before, from braver people.

partial.text: She laughs at the offer, but she tosses you a purse to go away.

success.text: {actor} lays it out: the kingdom will come for her sooner or later. She takes the offer, and rides for the border with whoever follows her.

options.label: Back away while you can
options.description: Break off while you still can. The lair stays.

outcome.text: You back away across the yard, and she lets you go.

start.text: Tents and banners fill a river meadow: a pretender's host, drilling with pikes. The banners bear a crown that isn't the kingdom's, and the sergeants are shouting themselves hoarse.

options.label: Slip in among the camp followers
options.description: Do it well and you strike with the Edge. Get spotted and you go in Exposed.

fail.text: A picket stops you at the edge of the meadow, and shouts for the officer of the watch.

partial.text: You get into the camp, but a sergeant is watching you.

success.text: {actor} blends in with the cooks and the washerwomen, and finds the pretender's tent before anyone asks a question.

options.label: Spread word the king's army is coming
options.description: Thin out the host before you strike. If it fails, they know your faces.

fail.text: Nobody believes you, and now the sergeants are looking for you.

partial.text: Some of the levies slip away in the night. Not enough.

success.text: {actor}'s rumour runs through the levies like fire. By morning half of them have deserted.

options.label: Walk in and ask for the commander

outcome.text: You walk up to the pickets openly, and they take you in.
You leave the meadow to the pretender and keep well clear of the pickets.

assault.text: The pretender's sworn men close around you: veterans in mismatched mail, and a sergeant who has done this before.

options.label: Fight
options.description: Success clears the lair. Do badly and they rally around their leader; fail and they drive you off, and the lair stays.

critFail.text: They ride you down in the meadow. You escape over the river with nothing but your lives.

fail.text: There are too many pikes. You break out of the camp and run, and the host cheers.

partial.text: You cut your way through the sworn men, but the pretender has seen the fight and is riding up.

success.text: The sworn men fall or yield, and without them the muster melts away. The pay-chest is still in the commander's tent.

options.label: Fire the supply wagons
options.description: Starve the host instead of fighting it. Getting caught hurts.

fail.text: {actor} is caught with the torch and beaten for it.

partial.text: The wagons smoulder, and the pretender rides up to see what's wrong.

success.text: {actor} gets a torch into the supply wagons. A host can't eat banners, and it starts to come apart.

options.label: Fall back to the river
options.description: Get out with a few cuts. The lair stays.

outcome.text: You fight your way back to the river and over it.

chief.text: The pretender rides up in borrowed armour, flanked by a standard-bearer, and demands to know who you serve.

options.label: Fight the pretender
options.description: Win and the lair is broken for good. Lose and you are driven off, and the lair stays.

fail.text: The pretender's guard closes ranks. {actor} goes down under the pikes, and you barely get them out.

partial.text: {actor} drags the pretender from the saddle, hurt badly in the doing. The host scatters.

success.text: The pretender falls, and the banner with them. The host is gone by morning, and the pay-chest with it, except for the part you took. In their tent: a silver service, pledged to buy a crown.

options.label: Convince them the cause is lost
options.description: Talk the host out of existence. No plunder, no bloodshed.

fail.text: 'Treason,' says the pretender, and the guards come for you.

partial.text: The pretender hears you out and lets you leave, which is more than you expected.

success.text: {actor} names the armies that will come, and the gallows at the end. The pretender listens, goes pale, and orders the banner struck.

options.label: Back away while you can
options.description: Break off while you still can. The lair stays.

outcome.text: You back off between the tents and lose yourselves among the camp followers.

start.text: An old battlefield cemetery, the markers tilted and the earth turned over as if from below. Mist lies on it at noon, and something walks between the graves.

options.label: Watch where they rise
options.description: Do it well and you strike with the Edge. Get spotted and you go in Exposed.

fail.text: Something in the mist sees you first.

partial.text: You see shapes in the mist, but no pattern.

success.text: {actor} watches the mist until the pattern shows: the dead rise around one great tomb, and only there.

options.label: Salt the gate and say the old words
options.description: Hold the dead back with the rites. Get them wrong and wake them all.

fail.text: {actor} gets the words wrong, and every grave in the place stirs.

partial.text: The words are only half remembered, and the dead only half held.

success.text: {actor} lays the salt line and speaks the words. The dead shy from the gate and come at you only one or two at a time.

outcome.text: You walk in through the lych-gate, and the mist closes behind you.
You back away from the gate. Nothing follows, this time.

assault.text: The dead rise around you: grey hands, rusted blades and mouths full of earth.

options.label: Fight
options.description: Success clears the lair. Do badly and they rally around their leader; fail and they drive you off, and the lair stays.

critFail.text: The dead drag you down in the mist. You crawl out with nothing but your lives.

fail.text: They keep coming, and their touch is cold as the grave. You fight your way out of the gate and run.

partial.text: You hack them down, torn and chilled, but they gather around the great tomb at the centre.

success.text: They fall and stay down. In the ossuary you find the grave-goods of a hundred soldiers, and the mist lifts.

options.label: Find the grave that wakes them
options.description: Strike at the heart of it. Opening the wrong grave hurts.

fail.text: {actor} pries at the wrong grave, and something inside bites.

partial.text: You find the tomb, and the dead follow you to it.

success.text: {actor} finds the broken seal on the great tomb. The other dead falter as you make for it.

options.label: Fall back to the gate
options.description: Get out with a few cuts. The lair stays.

outcome.text: You fight your way back to the gate, and the dead stop there.

chief.text: From the great tomb climbs a tall dead knight, still crowned with rust. The other dead turn to him and wait.

options.label: Fight the dead knight
options.description: Win and the lair is broken for good. Lose and you are driven off, and the lair stays.

fail.text: The knight's cold blade finds {actor}, and you drag them out of the gate.

partial.text: {actor} brings the knight down, chilled to the bone. The graveyard goes quiet.

success.text: The knight falls, and every grave in the place goes still. His tomb holds a king's ransom in rust, and some gold that isn't. Among the rust lies his old crown, worth more to the right buyer than all the coin.

options.label: Lay him to rest
options.description: Give the dead what they want. No grave-goods, but peace, and a lighter heart.

fail.text: He does not want rest. He wants company.

partial.text: He hesitates long enough for you to get out.

success.text: {actor} names him, and his battle, and his rest. He bows his head and lies down, and the graveyard sleeps with him.

options.label: Back away while you can
options.description: Break off while you still can. The lair stays.

outcome.text: You back away through the mist, and the dead let you go.

start.text: A manor house at the end of an overgrown drive, its shutters closed. Lamps burn in the cellar windows, and there are fresh cart-tracks right up to the door.

options.label: Look in at the cellar windows
options.description: Do it well and you strike with the Edge. Get spotted and you go in Exposed.

fail.text: {actor} knocks over a flowerpot, and the candles in the cellar go out all at once.

partial.text: You see robes and candles, but not how many.

success.text: {actor} creeps along the wall and counts them: a dozen robed figures, an altar, and a stair you can use.

options.label: Bluff your way in as new initiates
options.description: Walk in with the faithful. If they see through you, they're waiting.

fail.text: The doorkeeper asks a question you can't answer.

partial.text: The doorkeeper lets you in, but keeps a hand on her knife.

success.text: {actor} gives the right sign at the door, and you are welcomed in, smiling, down to the cellar.

outcome.text: You put a shoulder to the door, and it gives.

options.label: Leave the manor to its lamps

outcome.text: You leave the drive the way you came, and the lamps watch you go.

assault.text: Robed figures turn from the altar with knives out, still chanting. Something on the altar is moving.

options.label: Fight
options.description: Success clears the lair. Do badly and they rally around their leader; fail and they drive you off, and the lair stays.

critFail.text: The chant hits you like a fist. You flee the manor with nothing, and wake up far down the road.

fail.text: The knives and the chanting drive you back up the stair and out into the night.

partial.text: You cut down the first of them, but the high priest has reached the altar.

success.text: The cultists break and flee into the night. The cellar holds their offerings, and whatever was on the altar is dead.

options.label: Break the circle
options.description: Ruin the ritual. A circle does not like being broken.

fail.text: The circle bites back, and {actor} reels away with burnt hands.

partial.text: The circle breaks, and the chant changes.

success.text: {actor} scuffs the chalk circle and the chant falters. The cultists cry out and fall back to their priest.

options.label: Fall back up the stair
options.description: Get out with a few cuts. The lair stays.

outcome.text: You fight your way back up the cellar stair and out.

chief.text: The high priest raises a black knife over the altar, and the shadows in the cellar thicken into something with too many arms.

options.label: Fight the priest and the shadow
options.description: Win and the lair is broken for good. Lose and you are driven off, and the lair stays.

fail.text: The shadow wraps around {actor} and won't let go. You haul them out of the cellar.

partial.text: {actor} kills the priest, torn by the shadow before it fades. The cult is broken.

success.text: The priest falls, and the shadow with him. In his chambers you find the cult's purse and letters that would ruin half the town council. On the altar lies a carved idol, very old, that some collector would pay for.

options.label: Banish what they called
options.description: Send the thing home. Fail and it notices you.

fail.text: The shadow likes {actor}, and squeezes.

partial.text: The shadow withdraws, and so do you.

success.text: {actor} speaks the words backwards, and the shadow goes back where it came from, taking the priest with it.

options.label: Back away while you can
options.description: Break off while you still can. The lair stays.

outcome.text: You back up the stair and slam the cellar door behind you.

start.text: A stepped temple swallowed by vines, its stair carved with snakes. Masked worshippers come and go at dusk, and the air smells of incense and rot.

options.label: Climb the vines to a high window
options.description: Do it well and you strike with the Edge. Get spotted and you go in Exposed.

fail.text: A vine tears loose, and a masked guard looks up.

partial.text: You get in, but not quietly.

success.text: {actor} gets you up the vines and in through a high window, above the worshippers.

options.label: Steal masks from the bathing pool
options.description: Walk in masked. Get caught and the temple is roused.

fail.text: A worshipper catches {actor}'s wrist and screams.

partial.text: One mask is not enough to fool anyone for long.

success.text: {actor} lifts three masks while the worshippers bathe. You walk in among them.

outcome.text: You climb the great stair in plain sight. The worshippers watch you come.

options.label: Leave the temple to its snakes

outcome.text: You slip back into the jungle and leave the temple to its incense.

assault.text: Masked cultists close in with venom-blackened blades, and from the pit below comes a long, dry hiss.

options.label: Fight
options.description: Success clears the lair. Do badly and they rally around their leader; fail and they drive you off, and the lair stays.

critFail.text: The venom takes hold. You wake in the jungle with nothing, a day later.

fail.text: The venom slows you, and the blades keep coming. You stagger out into the jungle.

partial.text: You beat them back, scratched and sick with venom, and their priestess climbs out of the pit.

success.text: The cultists drop their blades and run. The temple's offerings are heaped in the shrine, and there are no more masks at dusk.

options.label: Drive the snakes back on them
options.description: Turn the temple's pets against it. Snakes bite.

fail.text: A temple snake bites {actor} on the hand.

partial.text: The snakes scatter in every direction, including yours.

success.text: {actor} knows what the temple snakes fear. Smoke and noise send them back into the worshippers.

options.label: Fall back down the stair
options.description: Get out with a few cuts. The lair stays.

outcome.text: You fight your way down the stair and into the trees.

chief.text: The temple's priestess comes up out of the pit with a serpent as thick as a man coiled about her shoulders.

options.label: Fight the priestess and her serpent
options.description: Win and the lair is broken for good. Lose and you are driven off, and the lair stays.

fail.text: The serpent wraps around {actor}, and you barely cut them free.

partial.text: {actor} is crushed and bitten, but the serpent dies and the priestess flees.

success.text: The serpent dies in the pit and the priestess with it. The temple's hoard of venom-gold is yours. In the serpent's nest, among the bones, lies an emerald as big as an egg.

options.label: Unmask her before the faithful
options.description: Turn the faithful against her. No hoard, but no more blood.

fail.text: The faithful hiss as one, and come at you.

partial.text: The faithful hesitate. You get out while they do.

success.text: {actor} tears the priestess's mask off and shows the faithful the frightened woman behind it. They tear off their own masks and run.

options.label: Back away while you can
options.description: Break off while you still can. The lair stays.

outcome.text: You back down the stair, and the serpent doesn't follow into daylight.

start.text: Deep in the wood a hut on stilts stands over black water, with three chimneys and one door. Charms of bone and hair hang from every branch, and they all turn to face you.

options.label: Read the charms before you go nearer
options.description: Do it well and you strike with the Edge. Get spotted and you go in Exposed.

fail.text: {actor} touches a charm, and it screams.

partial.text: The charms are a muddle. You cross carefully.

success.text: {actor} reads the charms and finds the gap in them. You cross the water unheard.

options.label: Leave a gift on the step
options.description: 10 gold. Hags love a gift, and are careless with those who bring them.

outcome.text: The coins vanish from the step. The door opens politely, and the crones are all smiles: you go in on your terms.

options.label: Ward yourselves with salt and iron (1 arcana)
options.description: Fey magic slides off a proper warding. You go in with the Edge, and their first curses miss.

outcome.text: You chalk the signs on your brows and hang cold iron at your throats. The charms in the trees turn away from you, one by one.
You wade the black water to the stilts, and something brushes your legs.
You leave the hollow, and for a mile the charms turn to watch you go.

assault.text: The water rises in grasping shapes, and the hut's door bangs open. Two crones cackle from the doorway while a third stirs the pot.

options.label: Fight
options.description: Success clears the lair. Do badly and they rally around their leader; fail and they drive you off, and the lair stays.

critFail.text: You wake on the road with your purses lighter and no memory of the last day.

fail.text: The water drags you under, again and again. You crawl out of the hollow half-drowned.

partial.text: You beat off the water-shapes, but the three crones are joining hands at the pot.

success.text: The crones shriek and flee into the bog, and the hut sinks after them. On the step you find the price of a hundred bad bargains.

options.label: Upset the cauldron
options.description: Spill their brew and their power with it. It burns.

fail.text: The brew splashes {actor}, and it burns like cold fire.

partial.text: The cauldron rocks and spills, and the crones turn on you.

success.text: {actor} leaps the rail and kicks over the pot. The brew hisses into the water, and the crones scream.

options.label: Fall back across the water
options.description: Get out with a few cuts. The lair stays.

outcome.text: You wade back across the black water as fast as you can.

chief.text: The three of them join hands, and the eldest grows tall and grey and terrible.

options.label: Fight the coven
options.description: Win and the lair is broken for good. Lose and you are driven off, and the lair stays.

fail.text: The eldest lifts {actor} like a child and throws them into the water. You run.

partial.text: {actor} is clawed and cursed, but the coven breaks and the hut sinks into the bog.

success.text: The coven breaks. The eldest falls and the others flee screaming into the bog. Their hut is full of payment for old bargains. Among the payment hangs an old saint's finger-bone in a silver case.

options.label: Strike a bargain to make them leave
options.description: Hags bargain. It always costs more than they say.

fail.text: They laugh, and the water rises around you again.

partial.text: They let you go, for now.

success.text: They agree to go, for a price: one of your happier memories, taken from whoever bargained. The hut walks off into the bog on its stilts.

options.label: Back away while you can
options.description: Break off while you still can. The lair stays.

outcome.text: You back away across the water while they argue over you.

start.text: Scorched rock and cracked bones litter the crag below a cave mouth. The herds have been gone from these slopes for a year, and now you can see why: a young drake suns itself on the ledge, and another stirs in the cave behind.

options.label: Climb up downwind
options.description: Do it well and you strike with the Edge. Get spotted and you go in Exposed.

fail.text: A stone clatters down the crag, and two heads turn your way.

partial.text: You get close, but one of the drakes lifts its head.

success.text: {actor} brings you up the rocks downwind, close enough to smell the brimstone, and the drakes are asleep.

options.label: Stake out a goat as bait
options.description: Draw them into the open. If they don't bite, they find you instead.

fail.text: The goat bleats, the drakes ignore it, and they see you instead.

partial.text: One drake takes the bait. The other watches from the ledge.

success.text: The drakes come down to fight over the goat in the open, and you are waiting.

outcome.text: You climb the crag in the open, and the drakes are waiting.
You leave the crag to the drakes and take the long way round.

assault.text: The drakes come down off the ledge in a rush of heat and leathery wings, snapping and spitting fire.

options.label: Fight
options.description: Success clears the lair. Do badly and they rally around their leader; fail and they drive you off, and the lair stays.

critFail.text: Fire catches your packs. You run down the crag with smoke trailing behind you.

fail.text: Fire and teeth drive you down the crag. You run until the heat is gone.

partial.text: You bring down one drake, burnt and bloodied, and a roar from the cave answers its death.

success.text: The drakes fall on the rocks. In the cave are the bones of a year's herds, and the bright things the drakes collected.

options.label: Lure them onto the loose scree
options.description: Let the mountain fight for you. Pick the wrong slope and you fall.

fail.text: The scree goes from under {actor} instead.

partial.text: The scree shifts, and so do you, up to the cave.

success.text: {actor} picks the scree slope that will move. The drakes slide down it in a roar of stone, and you climb past them to the cave.

options.label: Fall back down the crag
options.description: Get out with a few cuts. The lair stays.

outcome.text: You scramble down the crag with fire licking at your heels.

chief.text: From deep in the cave comes the brood-mother, bigger than both the others together, and very angry.

options.label: Fight the brood-mother
options.description: Win and the lair is broken for good. Lose and you are driven off, and the lair stays.

fail.text: Her fire catches {actor} full on. You drag them down the crag, smoking.

partial.text: {actor} is badly burnt, but the brood-mother falls. The roost is yours.

success.text: The brood-mother dies in her cave, and with her the roost. Her hoard is not large, but it is gold. In among it, one ruby the size of a thumb.

options.label: Drive her off with fire and noise
options.description: Make the roost not worth it. She keeps her hoard.

fail.text: She is not afraid of torches. She is made of fire.

partial.text: She backs into the cave, and you back away from it.

success.text: {actor} drives her back with torches and noise until she takes wing, screaming, for the high peaks. You take the gleanings of the nest.

options.label: Back away while you can
options.description: Break off while you still can. The lair stays.

outcome.text: You back away down the crag while she roars after you.

start.text: A hall of rough-hewn boulders, big enough to stable a ship, sits in the high pass. Cattle bones the size of benches are heaped by the door, and the smoke from the roof smells of roast ox.

options.label: Sneak in under the door
options.description: Do it well and you strike with the Edge. Get spotted and you go in Exposed.

fail.text: A giant's dog the size of a horse sniffs you out.

partial.text: You get in, but a giant child sees you and starts shouting.

success.text: {actor} leads you in under the gap at the bottom of the door, and you can walk under the table.

options.label: Challenge them to a riddle game
options.description: Giants love a contest. They are bad losers.

fail.text: They don't like losing, and they're bad losers.

partial.text: They play a few rounds and get bored.

success.text: {actor} keeps them riddling and drinking until half of them are snoring.

outcome.text: You hammer on the great door, and the hall goes quiet.
You leave the pass to the giants and go round by the low road.

assault.text: The giants come out roaring, swinging tree trunks, and the ground shakes with every step.

options.label: Fight
options.description: Success clears the lair. Do badly and they rally around their leader; fail and they drive you off, and the lair stays.

critFail.text: They kick you down the mountain like stones, and your packs go further than you do.

fail.text: A tree trunk sweeps you off the path. You crawl away down the scree.

partial.text: You bring one giant down, bruised all over, and their mother takes the great maul down from the hearth.

success.text: The giants fall in the pass like trees. Their hall holds the stolen tithes of three valleys.

options.label: Stampede their cattle into the hall
options.description: Use their own herd against them. Oxen this big hurt.

fail.text: A giant ox tramples {actor} into the mud.

partial.text: The cattle mill about, and so do the giants.

success.text: {actor} sets the giants' herd stampeding into the hall. The giants chase their dinner, and their mother is left alone.

options.label: Fall back down the pass
options.description: Get out with a few cuts. The lair stays.

outcome.text: You fight your way back down the pass, and they throw rocks after you.

chief.text: The clan's mother, grey-bearded and twice the height of the rest, takes down a great maul from over the hearth.

options.label: Fight the clan's mother
options.description: Win and the lair is broken for good. Lose and you are driven off, and the lair stays.

fail.text: The maul catches {actor}. You carry them down the pass.

partial.text: {actor} is battered half to death, but she falls, and the clan goes with her.

success.text: She falls across her own hearth, and the clan scatters to the high peaks. The steading's store is yours. Among the plunder: a cask of good wine, carried up the pass like a thimble.

options.label: Bargain: the high valleys for the low herds
options.description: Talk the clan into moving on. No plunder, no broken bones.

fail.text: She stops laughing.

partial.text: She laughs, and lets you go for the entertainment.

success.text: {actor} talks of greener valleys further up, with no soldiers in them. She thinks about it, then calls her clan together, and they leave the pass by nightfall.

options.label: Back away while you can
options.description: Break off while you still can. The lair stays.

outcome.text: You back out of the hall while she laughs at you.

start.text: A long grassy mound with a stone door in its end, pushed open from inside. Cold air breathes out of the dark, and the grass around the door is dead.

options.label: Study the door-carvings first
options.description: Knowing the barrow's plan gives you the Edge in its passages. Costs nothing but time.

fail.text: The carvings mean nothing to {actor}. You go in blind.

partial.text: {actor} makes out a name and a warning, and you go in wary.

success.text: {actor} reads the carvings: the barrow's plan, and the words that kept its lord asleep. You go in knowing the way.

outcome.text: You duck under the lintel, and the cold closes around you.
You leave the door as you found it, open, and walk away a little faster than you came.

passage.text: The passage slopes down between walls of dry stone, and the floor is a lattice of old bones. Some of the flagstones are not flagstones.

options.label: Pick a safe way through
options.description: Slow and careful. A good path brings you to the chamber with the Edge.

fail.text: A flag tips under {actor}, who drops into a pit of bones and climbs out torn.

partial.text: {actor} finds most of the false flags. Most.

success.text: {actor} finds every false flag, and you reach the burial chamber quiet and ready.

options.label: Rush through
options.description: Quick, but anything that goes wrong is loud.

fail.text: Flags give way under {actor}, and the noise echoes ahead of you into the chamber.

partial.text: {actor} gets through with a turned ankle.

success.text: {actor} dances over the false flags and you follow in their steps.

outcome.text: You climb back to the daylight. The barrow keeps its secrets.

guardian.text: In the burial chamber a dead lord sits up on his bier. His eyes are cold lights, and the bones on the floor stir at his word.

options.label: Fight the barrow lord
options.description: Win and the barrow's treasury is yours. Lose and you are driven out, and the barrow stays haunted.

fail.text: His cold blade and his rising dead drive you back up the passage and out into the light.

partial.text: You hack him down, torn and frozen, and the bones fall still.

success.text: {actor} strikes the lights from his eyes, and he falls back on his bier, only bones.

options.label: Lay him to rest
options.description: End it without a fight, and with a lighter heart. Failing angers him.

fail.text: He does not want rest. His cold hand closes on {actor}'s throat.

partial.text: He lies back slowly, and his cold hand brushes {actor} as he goes.

success.text: {actor} names him and speaks the rites over him. He lies back with a sigh, and the cold goes out of the barrow.

options.label: Ward the bier with salt and chalk (1 arcana)
options.description: Bind him inside a circle first, then speak the rites. Far easier, and the warding is spent either way.

fail.text: The chalk line smokes and breaks as he rises. {actor} is caught too close.

partial.text: He strains at the circle, then lies back, cursing {actor} in a dead tongue.

success.text: He rises, finds the circle, and cannot cross it. {actor} speaks the rites, and he lies back with a sigh.

options.label: Flee
options.description: Get out with a few cuts. The barrow stays haunted.

outcome.text: You run for the daylight with the dead at your heels.

vault.text: Behind the bier lies the barrow's treasury: grave-goods heaped around a sealed coffer, with a curse cut into its lid.

options.label: Take everything, coffer and all
options.description: The most loot, and the curse's sting.

outcome.text: You take it all. The curse bites as you lift the coffer, a cold that goes to the bone, but the gold and the gems are real.

options.label: Take the grave-goods and leave the coffer

outcome.text: You take what lies loose and leave the coffer to its curse. The barrow is quiet now, for good.

options.label: Break the curse, then take everything
options.description: All of it without the sting, if you can. A failure hurts.

fail.text: The curse lashes out at {actor}. Nobody wants to touch the coffer now.

partial.text: {actor} blunts the curse enough to open the coffer, if not to empty it.

success.text: {actor} unpicks the curse word by word, and the coffer opens on a lord's fortune.

start.text: An old mine adit, timbered and dark, with fresh tracks of small clawed feet going in and out. Someone has strung bells on a wire across the entrance.

options.label: Step over the bell-wire
options.description: Get in unheard, or ring their bells for them.

fail.text: {actor} brushes the wire. Bells ring, and far below little voices start yapping.

partial.text: You get past the wire, and find another just beyond it. Probably nobody heard.

success.text: {actor} spots the wire, and the second one behind it. You slip in unannounced.

options.label: Smoke them out through the airshafts
options.description: Thin them out before you go in. A botch warns them.

fail.text: The smoke draws the wrong way, out at you. The kobolds know you are coming.

partial.text: Some smoke goes down. You go in after it.

success.text: {actor} fires the airshafts. Half the tribe flees out of the far side of the hill, and the rest are coughing.

outcome.text: You leave the mine to the kobolds. The bells tinkle behind you in the wind.

gallery.text: The tunnels branch and branch again. The kobolds have been busy: deadfalls, sharpened stakes in the dark, and a rope bridge over a flooded shaft.

options.label: Find and spring their traps
options.description: Slow and careful. Done well, you arrive with the Edge.

fail.text: A deadfall catches {actor} across the shoulders.

partial.text: You spring most of them and walk around the rest.

success.text: {actor} springs every trap from a safe distance, and you reach the great working ready for them.

options.label: Cross the shaft on the rope bridge
options.description: The quick way. If it gives, you arrive wet, hurt and heard.

fail.text: The bridge was cut half through. {actor} goes into the black water and comes up gasping, and the splash carries.

partial.text: The bridge sways and holds. {actor} scrapes a shin on the far side.

success.text: You cross the shaft hand over hand, and come out right behind their chief's hall.

outcome.text: You feel your way back to the daylight. The yapping follows you.

warren.text: In the great working the kobolds have built a throne of ore-carts for their chief, who waves a lit oil lantern over his head. His whole tribe yaps around him, spears up.

options.label: Fight the chief and his tribe
options.description: Win and the mine is yours. Lose and they drive you out, and the mine stays theirs.

fail.text: Spears from every ledge, and then the lantern comes down in a sheet of fire. You flee back up the tunnels.

partial.text: You break the tribe in a long, scrappy fight, and the chief's lantern singes everyone.

success.text: {actor} knocks the lantern from the chief's claw, and the tribe breaks and scatters down the side shafts.

options.label: Hurl alchemist's fire at the throne (1 alchemicals)
options.description: Kobolds fear fire more than steel. An easier fight, and the flask is gone either way.

fail.text: The flask smashes on the rock wall and lights the ore-carts. Through smoke and spears you flee back up the tunnels.

partial.text: The throne goes up in green fire. The tribe scatters, but not before their spears find you.

success.text: {actor}'s flask bursts on the ore-cart throne. The chief and his tribe flee shrieking down every shaft at once.

options.label: Offer them a deeper mine elsewhere
options.description: Kobolds want a safe hole. Talk them into another one.

fail.text: The chief is not interested in your stories, and the spears come up.

partial.text: The chief takes a purse to think about it, and goes off to think somewhere else.

success.text: {actor} describes a deep, dark, empty mine three valleys over. The chief yaps orders, and the tribe packs up and leaves.

options.label: Flee
options.description: Get out with a few cuts. The mine stays theirs.

outcome.text: You run for the daylight with spears whistling past.

vault.text: Behind the throne lies the kobolds' hoard: ore, coin and the old miners' strongbox. A seam of silver glints in the wall above it.

outcome.text: You fill your packs from the hoard. With the tribe gone, the mine is just a mine again. The strongbox holds a fat uncut gem the old miners never sent to market.

options.label: Work the silver seam as well
options.description: A day's hard work for silver ore: heavy bars to carry home. The old timbers creak.

fail.text: The roof groans, and stones come down on {actor}. You take the hoard and get out.

partial.text: A day of hard work brings out a little silver ore, heavy as sin.

success.text: {actor} works the seam like an old miner. You leave with heavy packs: bars of rough silver, if you can carry them.

start.text: The shell of a keep stands on a mound, its towers fallen and its gatehouse choked with rubble. Below, the cellars are still roofed, and nobody has been down there for a long time.

options.label: Clear the rubble from the cellar stair
options.description: Hard work. A bad heave hurts, a slow one costs a day.

fail.text: The rubble shifts and rolls onto {actor}'s foot. You get in anyway, limping.

partial.text: It takes all day, but the stair is clear.

success.text: {actor} heaves the stones aside, and you go down fresh.

options.label: Look for another way in
options.description: A clever way in gives you the Edge below. A wrong guess costs a day.

fail.text: You find nothing, and in the end you dig after all. A wasted day.

partial.text: You find a postern, half blocked, and squeeze through.

success.text: {actor} finds the old postern stair and a garrison map scratched beside it. You go down knowing the way.

options.label: Leave the ruin to the crows

outcome.text: You leave the keep to the crows. It has waited this long.

undercroft.text: The cellars are half flooded and the vaulting cracked. Every sound brings down a trickle of grit, and there are rats, big ones.

options.label: Go carefully, testing every arch
options.description: Slow and safe, mostly. Done well, you reach the door with the Edge.

fail.text: An arch comes down without warning.

partial.text: You find a safe way, mostly, and reach the far end.

success.text: {actor} spots every cracked keystone, and the iron door at the end of the cellars.

options.label: Wade straight through
options.description: Quick and wet. The rats get their chance.

fail.text: {actor} goes under in a sinkhole and comes up with a rat on their arm.

partial.text: The rats take a bite or two out of {actor} on the way.

success.text: You splash through before the rats know you're there.

outcome.text: You climb back up into the light. The cellars can keep their secrets.

strongroom.text: At the end of the cellars is an iron door with a lock the size of a fist. Above it a carved face opens its stone eyes as you come near and asks, in a dry voice, for the word.

options.label: Give the warden the word
options.description: The house's old motto might do it. A wrong answer burns.

fail.text: {actor} guesses wrong. The face spits fire.

partial.text: {actor} gets it nearly right. The face scorches you all, then grudgingly lets you in.

success.text: {actor} remembers the old house's motto. The face closes its eyes, and the door swings open.

options.label: Pick the lock under its eyes
options.description: Quick fingers against a watchful warden.

fail.text: The face sees {actor}'s hands and spits fire on them.

partial.text: The lock gives, and so does the face's temper.

success.text: {actor} has the lock open before the face finishes asking.

outcome.text: You leave the face to its door and climb back to the light.

vault.text: The strongroom holds what the keep's last lord could not carry away: chests of old coin, a rack of rusted arms, and a ledger of debts owed to a family long dead.

outcome.text: You take the coin, and the lord's seal-ring, older than the keep, and leave the rest. The ruin has nothing more to give.

options.label: Read the ledger before you go
options.description: Old ledgers name old places. Mould wastes a day.

fail.text: The ledger is mould and old names. A day lost over it.

partial.text: {actor} reads of the lord's last days, and why he left.

effects.text: The ruined keep's last lord fled his debts in a single night, leaving his gold behind for fear of being followed.

success.text: {actor} finds a page about the lord's other holdings, and one of them is near.

effects.text: The ruined keep's ledger names another of its lord's old holdings.

start.text: A hut of stacked stone clings to the hillside, its roof heavy with turf and its door open. Inside, among bundles of scrolls and bottled oddities, an old man in a patched robe looks up from his reading, unsurprised. 'Visitors. Sit down, and mind the jars.'

options.label: Pay him to teach the old lore
options.description: 40 gold and 3 days. The best-suited of you without the skill learns it.

outcome.text: Three days of sigils, star-charts and his terrible tea. At the end of it, the patterns start to make sense.

options.label: Buy what he knows of the land
options.description: 10 gold. Marks 2 sites in this land on your map.

outcome.text: He takes your coin, unrolls a map that is mostly crossings-out, and marks two places with a burnt stick. 'Mind the second one.'

options.label: Trade tales of the old kingdoms for a lesson
options.description: Impress him and he teaches for free. Bore him and he lectures all night.

fail.text: {actor}'s stories are full of mistakes, and he corrects every one, until dawn.

partial.text: He won't teach, but he likes {actor}'s stories well enough to tell one back: of a ruin, and where it is.

success.text: He laughs until he coughs. 'You know more than you look. Very well, I'll teach one of you for nothing.'

outcome.text: He talks of the stars, the old kingdoms and the price of ink, and he gives you a bowl of something that was probably soup.

effects.text: The hermit says the old kingdoms buried their dead with their maps, so the dead would not get lost.

start.text: A cottage stands over a spring that bubbles up into a stone basin. Herbs dry in bunches under the eaves, and a woman with green-stained hands is grinding something pungent in a mortar. She looks at your wounds before she looks at your faces.

options.label: Pay her to tend your hurts
options.description: 12 gold and a day. She mends everyone and eases weariness.

outcome.text: Poultices, bitter tea and a night under her roof. You wake mended and clear-headed.

options.label: Pay to learn her craft
options.description: 30 gold and 3 days. The best-suited of you without the skill learns it.

outcome.text: Three days of roots, leaves and what not to mix with what. Her pupil leaves with green hands and a good deal of sense.

options.label: Gather herbs for her in the bog
options.description: A day's work for her care instead of gold. The bog has leeches.

fail.text: {actor} comes back with the wrong herbs and a leech on each leg. She tends you anyway, grudgingly.

partial.text: {actor} brings back enough. She pays in poultices.

success.text: {actor} brings back exactly what she needed, and some she didn't know grew here. She tends you all and won't take a coin.

options.label: Drink from the spring and rest a while
options.description: Free, but she only has the time once a month. Heals everyone a quarter of their HP and eases weariness.

outcome.text: The spring water is cold and sweet. You sit by the basin while she works, and leave rested.
She waves you off without looking up from her mortar.

effects.text: The herbwife says the spring never freezes, not even in the winter the river did.

twist.what: he isn't sparring: he wants one last real fight

start.text: A neat farmhouse with a sword hung over the door. In the yard a grey-haired man is practising cuts against a post with a walking stick. He stops when he sees your weapons, and smiles thinly.

options.label: Pay for lessons
options.description: 40 gold and 3 days. The best-suited of you without the skill learns it.

outcome.text: Three days of footwork in the yard until his pupil can do it in their sleep, and does, twitching.

options.label: Spar with him for the privilege
options.description: Impress him and he teaches for free. He doesn't pull his blows.

fail.text: He puts {actor} on the ground three times without breaking a sweat. 'Come back when you're quicker.'

twist.text: He puts {actor} on the ground, then keeps hitting, and he isn't smiling.

partial.text: {actor} lasts long enough to earn a few bruises and his grudging respect. He teaches, between insults.

twist.text: Halfway through, he swaps the stick for a blade, and his eyes go flat.

success.text: {actor} touches him twice. He laughs, bows, and teaches for nothing.

twist.text: {actor} touches him twice. He stops laughing, and takes down the sword from over the door.

options.label: Read the old man
options.description: Insight shows how likely he is to want more than a lesson. Misreading him puts you off.

fail.text: {actor} can't make him out, and feels foolish for trying.

partial.text: There is something hungry behind his smile. {actor} can't say how hungry.

success.text: {actor} sees it clearly: he misses it, the real thing. How much is plain on his face.

options.label: Ask where the outlaws lie up
options.description: 10 gold. Marks 2 lairs in this land on your map.

outcome.text: He was a road-warden once. He takes your coin and draws two camps in the dust with his stick.

options.label: Talk old fights over a cup

outcome.text: He pours something strong and tells you of duels in courts that no longer exist. He is lonely, you think.

effects.text: The old duelist says every sword-school in the old capital taught the same trick, and none of them admitted it.

duel.text: The old duelist salutes with a real sword. 'One more, before I'm too old to hold it. To first blood, or further.'

options.label: Cross swords with him
options.description: Give him his fight. Win and he teaches for nothing.

fail.text: He is old, and he is still better. {actor} falls in the dust, and he walks away without looking back.

partial.text: Blood on both sides. He lowers the sword, satisfied, and teaches {actor} what he knows while they heal.

success.text: {actor} disarms him. He laughs until he weeps, and teaches you everything he knows.

options.label: Talk him down
options.description: Remind him who he was. Fail and he comes on.

fail.text: He doesn't hear {actor}. He hears the sword.

partial.text: He lowers the blade, ashamed, and asks you to go.

success.text: {actor} talks of the duels he already won. He sits down hard, and in the end he teaches after all.

outcome.text: You turn your backs on him. He doesn't follow, and he doesn't watch you go.

start.text: A thin tower of grey stone with a glass room at its top. Maps cover every wall inside, pinned three deep, and a stooped woman with ink to the elbows peers at you over her spectacles. 'Travellers! Where have you been? Tell me everything.'

options.label: Buy a copy of her best map
options.description: 15 gold. Marks 3 sites in this land on your map.

outcome.text: She sells you a copy, still wet, and taps three places on it. 'Those aren't on anyone else's.'

options.label: Trade what you've seen for what she knows
options.description: Your road knowledge for hers. Nothing lost but breath.

fail.text: She corrects {actor} on every road you name, and gives nothing back but a sniff.

partial.text: {actor}'s roads are worth something to her. She marks one place for you in return.

success.text: {actor} tells her of roads she has never mapped. She is delighted, and marks two places on your map.

options.label: Pay her to teach you the old borders
options.description: 30 gold and 2 days. The best-suited of you without the skill learns it.

outcome.text: Two days over old maps: borders, roads and kingdoms that are gone. Her pupil will never look at a ruin the same way.

options.label: Copy her maps while she isn't looking
options.description: Free, if she doesn't catch you. If she does, she charges.

fail.text: She catches {actor} at it, and charges for the ink before she throws you out.

partial.text: {actor} gets a corner of one map before she turns round.

success.text: {actor} copies two sheets while she makes tea. She never knows.

outcome.text: She shows you her latest map, and tells you everything wrong with everyone else's.

effects.text: The cartographer says half the roads on the kingdom's maps were drawn by men who never left the capital.

start.text: A log lodge in the deep wood, antlers over the door and hides stretched to dry. The old woman on the step has one good eye and a bow across her knees, and a hound that hasn't decided about you yet.

options.label: Pay her to teach you the woods
options.description: 35 gold and 3 days. The best-suited of you without the skill learns it.

outcome.text: Three days in the woods with her, eating what she finds and sleeping where she says. Her pupil comes back knowing the land.

options.label: Go hunting with her
options.description: Keep up and she teaches for free. Two days either way.

fail.text: {actor} spots nothing she hasn't already seen. Two days of walking, and a long silence on the way back.

partial.text: You don't impress her, but on the hunt she shows you the tracks of something much bigger than a deer.

success.text: {actor} spots the stag before she does. She grunts, which is praise, and teaches the slowest of you what she knows.

options.label: Ask what has been killing the herds
options.description: 8 gold. Marks 2 lairs in this land on your map.

outcome.text: She takes the coin without thanks and tells you where the killers sleep. 'Go if you want. I'm too old.'

options.label: Share her fire
options.description: Free, but she only shares it once a month. Heals everyone a quarter of their HP and eases weariness.

outcome.text: She shares her fire and her stew, and says almost nothing. It is the best night's sleep you've had in weeks.
She nods once, and goes back to her snares.

effects.text: The old huntress says the wolves have stopped howling this year, and that is worse.

start.text: A coaching inn by the old road, its doors hanging open. The tables are still laid and the plates furred with dust, as if everyone stood up in the middle of supper and walked out together.

options.label: Search the rooms
options.description: Someone left in a hurry. They may have left clues.

fail.text: {actor} finds nothing but dust, and a feeling of being watched from the stairs.

partial.text: In the strongbox under the bar {actor} finds a few coins, and the guest ledger.

effects.text: The waystation's guest ledger ends mid-entry on the night of a red moon. Someone, somewhere, is still waiting for the people who signed it. (A quest hook: quests arrive in a later plan.)

success.text: {actor} finds the strongbox, the ledger, and a coachman's route-map with one stop circled in red ink.

effects.text: The waystation's guest ledger ends mid-entry on the night of a red moon. Someone, somewhere, is still waiting for the people who signed it. (A quest hook: quests arrive in a later plan.)

options.label: Sleep in the old beds
options.description: A day, for a roof and a proper bed.

outcome.text: The beds are dusty but dry. Nobody comes in the night, though the doors bang until dawn.
You close the door behind you, for whatever good it does.

start.text: A door of green bronze is set into the hillside, taller than three men, without handle or keyhole. Words run around its frame in a script you half know, and the turf over it has never been cut.

options.label: Read the words around the frame
options.description: The door says what it is waiting for, to those who can read it.

fail.text: The script slides away from {actor}'s eyes. It means nothing, today.

partial.text: {actor} makes out enough to know what the door is waiting for.

effects.text: The bronze door asks for a key: three things that belonged to three dead kings. (A quest hook: quests arrive in a later plan.)

success.text: {actor} reads it all: what the door wants, and where the first of the three kings lies buried.

effects.text: The bronze door asks for a key: three things that belonged to three dead kings. (A quest hook: quests arrive in a later plan.)

options.label: Lay a hand on the bronze and listen
options.description: Magic holds it shut. It may not like being touched.

fail.text: The bronze bites {actor} with cold, and the hand stays numb for an hour.

partial.text: {actor} feels something vast and patient on the other side, and takes the hand away quickly.

success.text: {actor} feels the ward's shape, and something behind it that is glad of company. You leave strangely heartened.

options.label: Leave the door to its waiting

outcome.text: You leave the door as it has always been. It doesn't seem to mind.
